mappings.note: A quoted speech is given and the pupil must conclude what it reveals about Dhyan Chand - examining a text closely and drawing a conclusion, LO-7. Rejected LO-6, which is skimming for the gist.
Why people began calling him 'hockey ka jadugar' - the cause must be picked out from the text among four plausible options. LO-7.
Who bears that title - a specific point in the lesson. LO-7.
The year (1933) is a stated detail. LO-7, not LO-6.
The author's year of birth is stated in the memoir. LO-7.
Which regiment he played for - a stated detail. LO-7.
Which team tried to snatch the ball - a specific point in the text. LO-7.

Match-the-following glossing military and sporting terms (Lance Naik, Berlin Olympic, Punjab Regiment, Sappers and Miners, Subedar) - unfamiliar words and their meanings, LO-10. Rejected LO-7: the work is lexical, not about the memoir's events.
Gadyansh with three sub-questions, including identifying the source and the speaker of 'main' - sustained close reading, LO-7.
Gadyansh with five MCQ sub-questions on the revenge episode - close reading for specific points, LO-7.
Gadyansh on his 'success mantra' with three sub-questions - close reading, LO-7.
Gadyansh on his birth and enlistment with five sub-questions - close reading for specific points, LO-7.
Gadyansh on the Berlin Olympic captaincy with three sub-questions - close reading, LO-7.
Asks which of Dhyan Chand's qualities the pupil will try to adopt - writing one's own response after reading, LO-17. Rejected LO-7: the answer is the pupil's, not the text's.

'kaise?' asks the pupil to argue that his name is unforgettable, drawing on the lesson and their own view - reading with understanding and offering an opinion, LO-8. Rejected LO-7, which would cover only locating the facts.
His qualities as a player are gathered from the text - locating points, LO-7.

Explication of the closing aphorism about a wrongdoer's fear - drawing out the sense of a sentence, LO-7. Rejected LO-15, which covers lay-tuk, chhand, muhavare and lokokti, whereas this is a plain-prose maxim of the author's own.
Explication of quoted lines to show what they reveal of his temperament - inference from close reading, LO-7.
The secret of his success (lagan, sadhana, khel bhavna) is stated in the text. LO-7.
Asks which details show he put others first - evidence-gathering and conclusion, LO-7.
'If you were in his place, would you take revenge, and how?' - the pupil writes their own considered response, LO-17. Rejected LO-7 as nothing in the text answers it.
Why the Miners player struck him is stated in the passage. LO-7.
When and how he began playing hockey - stated details. LO-7. NB the printed key is wrong: it says Major Tiwari urged him to play CRICKET, where the lesson says hockey.
Why he received the title - the cause is given in the text. LO-7.
'What does the lesson teach us' asks for the whole text's message - LO-6, guessing the vishayvastu of a composition, rather than LO-7's specific point.

Names the lesson's genre (sansmaran). LO-9 is the outcome about reading compositions of various kinds, which is what genre recognition rests on. Rejected LO-7, since no content of the memoir is at stake.
Which regiment in 1933 - a stated detail. LO-7.
Which team's player struck him - a stated detail. LO-7.
How he took his revenge (six goals) is stated. LO-7.
His moolmantra is stated in the text. LO-7.
'nausikhiya shabd se aap kya samajhte hain' is a word-meaning question - LO-10. Rejected LO-7: nothing of the memoir's content is being located.
His army rank at the Berlin Olympics is stated. LO-7.
The medal won at Berlin is stated in the text. LO-7.

General-awareness recall (his birthday as Rashtriya Khel Divas) that the memoir itself does not state. Cited at competency level because the Hindi frame has no information-seeking outcome at all - C-HIN2.2 is the reading-for-understanding competency, and its three outcomes cover opinion-giving, genre reading and dictionary use, none of which is this. Rejected LO-7, whose object is a point inside the given text.

General-awareness recall (whom the Khel Ratna is named after), again not stated in the memoir. Competency-level C-HIN2.2 for the same reason as the previous item; rejected LO-5, since nothing is being retold from radio, TV or newspaper in the pupil's own words.
What he did to avenge the injury - stated in the passage. LO-7.
Near-duplicate of the 'secret of success' item and mapped the same way: a stated point, LO-7.
